page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-metal is a bare-metal server configured with 288 dedicated vCPUs (144 physical cores with 2 threads per core) based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor clocked at up to 4.2 GHz. The system includes 504 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography extensions (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). Memory capacity stands at 2232.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 6 GHz, yielding approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per physical core. The bare-metal platform does not bundle any local storage, nor does it include GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded performance and memory throughput. The system achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core tests (313,057.86) and PassMark CPU metrics, including an extended instructions score of 381,577.31 and an encryption score of 328,886.3. Memory bandwidth reaches 1,090.07 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 412.54 GB/sec for writes. The instance excels at high-concurrency tasks, producing 423.02 million Redis SET operations per second and 174.2 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Compute compilation in Clang and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also place in the top decile. In contrast, single-core stress-ng performance falls into the middle tier, and CPU-based LLM token generation on smaller models shows limited efficiency.

Given its massive physical core count and over 2 TB of high-speed DDR5 memory, the c4-highmem-288-metal offers significant resource density for heavy compute and memory-bound footprints on dedicated bare metal. Because there is no included local storage, external network storage solutions must be provisioned. The server is well suited for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale Redis deployments, massive software compilation pipelines, and parallel data analytics engines.
